5.19 CKD / ESKD composites & time variables
Ported from ICI-CKD §5.14. Variable names are kept identical to the source project — including eskd_defination_1 and the _after_ici suffix on the ESRD variables — so the two projects stay directly comparable. In this project the _after_ici suffix means “after baseline_sample_date”, i.e. after first platinum.


Code
final_master <- final_master %>%
  mutate(
    eskd_composite = ifelse(esrd_kt_after_ici == 1 | eskd_defination_1 == 1, 1L, 0L),
    eskd_composite = ifelse(is.na(eskd_composite), 0L, eskd_composite),
    eskd_composite_date = pmin(esrd_kt_after_ici_date, eskd_defination_1_date,
                               na.rm = TRUE),

    time_to_eskd_composite  = as.numeric(eskd_composite_date  - baseline_sample_date),
    time_to_ckd_incidence   = as.numeric(ckd_incidence_date   - baseline_sample_date),
    time_to_ckd_progression = as.numeric(ckd_progression_date - baseline_sample_date),

    ckd_composite = ifelse(eskd_composite == 1 | ckd_incidence == 1 |
                           ckd_progression == 1, 1L, 0L),
    ckd_composite = ifelse(is.na(ckd_composite), 0L, ckd_composite),
    time_to_ckd_composite = pmin(time_to_eskd_composite,
                                 time_to_ckd_incidence,
                                 time_to_ckd_progression, na.rm = TRUE),

    last_cre_days  = as.numeric(last_cre_date - baseline_sample_date),
    aki_before_ckd = ifelse(!is.na(aki_days) & !is.na(time_to_ckd_composite) &
                            aki_days <= time_to_ckd_composite, 1L, 0L)
  )

2.2 Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)
Ported from the ICI-CKD project and built in Sections 5.16–5.19 of Data Management. Creatinine for these comes from the newer 2022P001091 RPDR pull.

These are the only outcomes on this page that are not censored at 90 days. A qualifying CKD episode has to be sustained for ≥ 90 days, so they run over the full length of RPDR creatinine follow-up rather than the 90-day window used by every model above and below. They are reported descriptively here and are not in any Fine-Gray, cause-specific or Cox model.

aki is also not the same variable as AKI_g2_90days / AKI_kdigo_90days: it compares each creatinine against the patient’s own preceding 90-day median (or 2-day low), across the whole record, rather than against a fixed pre-baseline value inside 90 days. The cross-tabulation below shows how far the two diverge.
📄 Download Word table


Code
.kid_row <- function(flag, time_var, label) {
  n <- sum(dat[[flag]] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  tt <- if (!is.null(time_var) && time_var %in% names(dat))
          dat[[time_var]][dat[[flag]] == 1] else NA_real_
  tibble::tibble(
    Outcome = label,
    `n (%)` = sprintf("%d (%.1f%%)", n, 100 * n / nrow(dat)),
    `Median days to event (IQR)` = if (n > 0 && any(!is.na(tt)))
        sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", median(tt, na.rm = TRUE),
                quantile(tt, .25, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(tt, .75, na.rm = TRUE))
      else "-"
  )
}

title: Ritu Project — Local/Early Stage Cohort Summary
text:
Long-Horizon Kidney Outcomes (CKD / ESKD / AKI)
Ported from the ICI-CKD project, re-anchored to baseline_sample_date. These are the only outcomes in the project that are not censored at 90 days — a qualifying CKD episode must be sustained for ≥ 90 days, so they use the full length of RPDR creatinine follow-up (median 446 days, max 1167).

esrd_kt (ESRD / KT at or before baseline, n = 1) is a Table 1 row.
These are reported descriptively and are not in any Fine-Gray, cause-specific or Cox model — mixing a full-follow-up outcome into the 90-day competing-risks framework would need its own censoring and competing-event decisions.
aki is a different variable from the existing AKI_g2_90days / AKI_kdigo_90days: it compares each creatinine against the patient’s own preceding 90-day median across the whole record, not against a fixed pre-baseline value inside 90 days. In the whole cohort they agree on 19 patients, aki alone flags 44, and AKI_kdigo_90days alone flags 14.
